title: Deploy gate design sketches: error-budget-aware CI/CD controls (warn-only -> enforced)
content:
Context / what this doc is
- We’re formalizing error budget policy (Hosted vs Dedicated) and need deploy-time controls that prevent making a bad situation worse.
- This is a rough sketch doc for the CI/CD “deploy gate” behavior tied to budget state: warn-only phase, then enforced release freeze for non-emergency changes.
- Assumption: budget state is computed centrally (SLO toolkit / budget computation job) and is queryable by tier + region + endpoint class.

Primary goals
1) Make budget impact visible at deploy time (warn-only first).
2) Provide an enforceable release freeze when budgets are exhausted (or burning fast) for the relevant tier.
3) Make it easy to ship emergency fixes + rollbacks even during freezes.
4) Keep the implementation simple enough to roll out gradually without blocking critical fixes early.

Non-goals (for this phase)
- We are NOT doing model-level gating (too much cardinality / too many owners).
- We are NOT gating customer-specific Dedicated accounts in CI in phase 1 (we’ll do per-tier / per-region first; customer-specific gates likely come later in console + SRE workflows).
- We are NOT building a full “change risk prediction” system; this is policy enforcement based on error budget state.


Sketch #1: How the gate fits into the deploy pipeline

(Developer PR) -> (CI build/test) -> (Release candidate) -> (Deploy step) -> (Canary) -> (Rollout)
                                                          |
                                                          +--> [SLO Gate Check]

Gate inputs
- service being deployed (e.g., api-gateway, routing-policy-eval, serving-request-path, telemetry pipelines)
- target environment (prod / staging)
- target regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west, etc.)
- affected tier(s): Hosted shared vs Dedicated reserved
- change type: feature, perf, infra, config-only, rollback

Gate decision
- PASS: proceed normally
- WARN: proceed but post a warning + log/annotation
- BLOCK: require override OR require rollback-only OR require emergency-fix workflow


Sketch #2: Mapping services -> budget scopes (blast radius)

We need a deterministic mapping that answers:
“Which SLO budgets might this deploy impact?”

Proposed simple mapping table (config file in repo; keep it conservative):
- api-gateway:
  - affects: Hosted + Dedicated
  - regions: whatever the deploy targets
  - endpoint classes: chat/completions, embeddings, streaming
- routing/control-plane policy evaluation:
  - affects: Hosted + Dedicated
  - endpoint classes: primarily chat/completions + streaming
- model serving request path (runtime):
  - affects: Hosted + Dedicated
  - endpoint classes: chat/completions, embeddings, streaming
- observability pipelines (metrics ingestion/aggregation):
  - affects: reporting quality; does NOT block deploy unless it degrades SLI computation integrity (separate “data quality gate”, future)

Notes
- Dedicated impacts are trickier because in theory a change could only impact some dedicated pools. For now, treat as “Dedicated tier overall in region” unless the deploy system knows the pool/account routing.
- We should avoid “global stop the world” gates. Prefer: only block deploys targeting the same region(s) with exhausted budgets.


Sketch #3: Budget states and gate behavior

Terminology
- Budget window: rolling 30d (canonical), with burn-rate alerts on shorter windows.
- “Budget remaining”: % error budget left (0% means exhausted).
- “Burning”: multi-window burn-rate indicates that if we keep going we’ll exhaust budget soon.

State machine (rough)
A) GREEN: budget remaining > X AND not burning
B) YELLOW: budget remaining <= X OR mild burn-rate
C) RED: budget remaining <= 0 OR severe burn-rate

Proposed defaults (tune with SRE)
- X = 25% remaining (early warning)
- Severe burn-rate = alert firing at “fast burn” thresholds (e.g., 2% budget in 1h and/or 5% in 6h style multi-window)

Gate policy (phase 1: warn-only)
- GREEN: PASS
- YELLOW: WARN (post Slack + annotate deploy)
- RED: WARN + require explicit acknowledgement (still allow)  [goal: no surprises, but don’t block while we calibrate]

Gate policy (phase 2: enforced)
- GREEN: PASS
- YELLOW: WARN
- RED:
  - BLOCK for change types: feature / perf / refactor / infra (non-mitigations)
  - ALLOW for:
    1) rollback
    2) emergency fix (requires override reason + on-call approval)
    3) mitigation configs (traffic shaping, fallback changes) if tagged as mitigation


Sketch #4: Override + approvals

We need a mechanism that:
- is auditable (who, when, why)
- is hard enough to discourage “just override it”
- is not so hard that we can’t recover during incidents

Override types
1) Acknowledge-only (warn-only phase)
   - developer checks box / provides reason string
   - logs to CI output + Slack notification
2) Emergency override (enforced phase)
   - requires:
     - reason
     - incident link OR “no incident yet” justification
     - approval by on-call (SRE primary OR service owner on-call)

Approval mechanism (rough options)
Option A: Slack-based approval
- CI posts to #eng-sre-oncall or #release-approvals with a short message
- on-call reacts with ✅ + bot verifies approver is in on-call group
- pros: fastest
- cons: more moving parts, needs bot hardening

Option B: Break-glass token
- on-call generates time-limited token (15 min) via internal tool
- token entered into CI to proceed
- pros: explicit, auditable
- cons: more friction

Current lean (suggested): Option B for enforced phase; Option A can be added later.

What gets recorded (minimum)
- deploy id, commit sha, service, regions, tier scopes evaluated
- budget state snapshot (budget remaining %, burning yes/no, timestamp)
- override reason + incident link (if any)
- approver identity
- a “post-action required” checkbox (e.g., if override used, auto-create follow-up task)


Sketch #5: Rollback allowances (very important)

Policy principle
- The gate should never prevent rollbacks.

How to detect rollback deploys
- best: deploy system explicitly marks a deploy as rollback (e.g., “rollback to previous stable”)
- okay: commit message tag [rollback] or release tooling flag

Edge case: roll-forward fix
- Sometimes the fastest fix is a roll-forward (new commit) rather than rollback.
- That’s fine, but it should go through emergency override flow during RED.


Sketch #6: Interaction with canaries and progressive delivery

We don’t want to block a canary that is intended to mitigate.

Proposed logic
- Gate check is done before starting canary.
- If RED and deploy is non-emergency => block.
- If RED and deploy is emergency/rollback => allow, but force smaller canary + faster health evaluation.

Additional safety knobs (optional)
- During RED: cap canary max traffic (e.g., 1% -> 5% max) unless override includes “expanded canary ok”.
- During RED: require automated rollback hooks to be enabled.


Sketch #7: Where the budget state comes from

We need a reliable, low-latency source of truth.

Candidate sources
1) Budget computation job output (e.g., stored in TSDB + exported)
2) SLO toolkit API (thin wrapper)
3) Prometheus query direct from CI (avoid if possible; brittle credentials, query latency)

Preferred for gating
- SLO toolkit API endpoint:
  GET /slo/v1/budgets/current?tiers=hosted,dedicated&regions=us-east,eu-west&classes=chat,embeddings,streaming
  returns a single snapshot for those scopes.

Important: keep response small and stable
- We should not return per-model/per-route values in the gating path.
- Response should be cacheable for ~60s to avoid thundering herd when multiple deploys happen.

Failure modes / fallbacks
- If the budget API is down:
  - phase 1: WARN and proceed
  - phase 2: default policy should be “WARN and proceed” OR “BLOCK non-emergency”? (open question)
  - SRE preference is usually “fail open” for tooling dependencies, but for a freeze policy we may choose “fail safe” for non-emergency.
  - propose: fail open for 48h after rollout, then revisit.


Sketch #8: Tier/region scoping rules (avoid over-blocking)

Rule of thumb
- Only block the deploy if it targets the same region(s) and the same tier(s) whose budget is RED.

Examples
- Dedicated eu-west is RED; Hosted us-east is GREEN.
  - a deploy targeting only us-east => PASS/WARN only
  - a deploy targeting eu-west => block for non-emergency

Service-specific nuance
- Some services are global (control plane) even if deployed regionally.
- If a “global” deploy can affect routing behavior in multiple regions, consider treating it as affecting all regions.
- We need an explicit flag in the service->scope mapping: scope_mode = regional | global.


Sketch #9: What this looks like in CI output (developer UX)

WARN example
- “SLO gate: Dedicated eu-west is YELLOW (budget remaining 18%). Proceeding (warn-only).”
- Link to:
  - tier SLO dashboard
  - current burn-rate alerts (if any)
  - runbook: error budget breach mitigation

BLOCK example (enforced)
- “SLO gate: Hosted us-east is RED (budget exhausted; severe burn-rate). Non-emergency deploy blocked.”
- Options:
  1) mark as rollback
  2) request emergency override (reason + token)
  3) retarget deploy to unaffected region(s)


Sketch #10: What qualifies as “mitigation config”

We’ll get pressure to allow “routing/fallback adjustments” even in RED.
We should explicitly enumerate mitigation-safe changes.

Mitigation-safe categories (initial)
- traffic shaping / overload shedding thresholds
- fallback policy config (e.g., route from Model A to compatible Model B)
- rate limit tightening for abusive patterns (if it reduces load)
- reducing max tokens defaults (if approved)

Not mitigation-safe by default
- enabling new model variants for general traffic
- turning on new batching mode globally
- widening concurrency limits

Implementation detail
- mitigation changes should be tagged in the deploy metadata (e.g., deploy_reason=mitigation + link to runbook step).
- Still require WARN + annotation so we can correlate with SLO recovery.


Open questions / TODOs
1) Fail-open vs fail-closed when budget API is unreachable (esp. in enforced phase).
2) How we classify “service owners” for approval routing (SRE only vs service on-call).
3) Granularity for Dedicated: do we eventually gate by customer account/pool? If yes, how does CI know which accounts are impacted?
4) Data quality: do we need a separate gate for “SLI computation broken” (missing tier tags, missing metrics)?
5) Do we need a “timeboxed freeze” (e.g., RED -> freeze automatically lifts after 6h if recovered) vs purely based on state?

Implementation notes (quick)
- ENG-4935: ship warn-only gate in CI; log overrides; Slack notify #eng-sre.
- ENG-4941: enforce freeze when budget exhausted; add emergency override.
- Should align with SLO config schema loader (PR-28438) so tiers/regions/classes are canonical.

Notes to self (Jordan)
- Keep first pass painfully simple: map a handful of critical services + prod only.
- Biggest risk is political/operational: people will try to label everything as mitigation. We need clear audit + consequences.
- Make sure rollback detection is bulletproof before enforcement flips on.
